glass.value: prefers-reduced-transparency → solid var(--surface), no blur; prefers-contrast: more → solid var(--surface) + var(--ink) border

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: CSS transitions: chips, slot moves (480ms), dock reveal (360ms), fullscreen inset (360ms), scrim (300ms).

motion.name: spring-model
motion.value: stiffness = (2π / response)²; friction = 4π · damping / response; mass 1; substeps ≤ 1/240s; frame dt capped at 1/30s
motion.purpose: Apple-style {damping, response} springs; always start from current value and velocity, so any animation is interruptible and retargetable.

motion.name: spring-move
motion.purpose: Travel: fullscreen FLIP, dock flights, avatar slow release, anchor changes.

motion.name: spring-sheet
motion.purpose: Spotlight grows from its origin (scale 0.5 → 1, opacity p × 1.6, scrim tracks p) and shrinks back.

motion.name: spring-fling
motion.purpose: Avatar thrown faster than 300px/s; small bounce carries momentum.

motion.name: spring-fade
motion.purpose: Spotlight under reduced motion: opacity only.

motion.name: project
motion.purpose: Where a flung avatar would coast to; picks the nearest anchor.

motion.name: rubberband
motion.purpose: Resistance when dragging the avatar past the safe area.

motion.value: scale(0.97), 100ms ease-out on :active (.nx-press, .chip, avatar); avatar drag scale(1.04)

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Anchor picker opening from its button.

motion.name: bubble
motion.value: 200ms ease from scale(0.96), origin at the avatar side; types 18ms/char; stays 6s, held on hover

motion.name: ascii-move
motion.purpose: Border flickers back to ASCII while a widget travels.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: springs → jumps or 150–220ms opacity fades; dock flights skipped; picker/bubble/dock lose transform

narrative.overview:
Nexus OS is a desk of warm paper with a faint dot grid, and on it sit a few cards the agent placed for you. Nothing on the desk is decoration. ASCII is how things move and how things are marked: a card draws its border corner to corner, types its content in, then settles into a clean edge; apps are named by small bracket glyphs like `[=]`; the agent's face is two lines of characters. At rest the screen should almost disappear.

The shell has two materials. Widgets are flat paper cards. The chrome that floats above them (menu bar, dock, Spotlight, the avatar and its bubble) is light frosted glass, so the dot field shows through softly and you can tell at once what is content and what is the system. A popover that opens inside glass is solid paper, never more glass.

Motion follows Apple's interaction model. Every press responds on pointer-down. Travel uses springs described by damping and response; they start from wherever a thing is now, keep its velocity when interrupted, and things leave along the path they came in. With reduced motion, travel becomes a short fade or a jump, and the ASCII build is skipped.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper neutrals with one teal accent, mirrored for dark mode
Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono for labels, keys, glyphs and every ASCII frame
Fixed 6×4 grid of 160px cells; the system picks geometry, never the user
ASCII frames for enter, move and exit; clean borders at rest
Glass only on floating chrome; solid under reduced transparency or high contrast

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal marks focus, selection and the agent at work. It is never decorative, and no second hue joins it. Errors use ink and an `x` mark, not red.

rules.name: The Two-Layer Rule
rules.body: Widgets are flat paper; only floating chrome is glass. Glass never sits on glass: the dock hides while Spotlight is open, and popovers inside glass (anchor picker, dock hint) are solid card.

rules.name: The ASCII-Born Rule
rules.body: Things enter, move and leave through ASCII frames, and the system marks things in characters (`[=]`, `>`, `x`, the face). The clean border is the resting state, not the default render.

rules.name: The Same-Path Rule
rules.body: Things leave the way they came. Spotlight grows out of whatever opened it (the ⌘K button, the dock's apps chip, the avatar) and shrinks back into it, returning focus there. Minimized apps fly into their dock chip and back to their cell; fullscreen grows from and returns to its cell; the dock slides down past the edge it rose from.

dos: Do start every press response on pointer-down (scale .97).
Do animate travel with springs that start from the current value and hand velocity off between gestures.
Do let things exit along the path they entered and return focus to what opened them.
Do fall back to solid card under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, and add an ink border under `prefers-contrast: more`.
Do replace travel with a short fade or a jump under reduced motion.
Do show honest system state ("engine local", "mic off") instead of invented numbers.
Do mark state with characters and ink (`x`, a border) before reaching for color.
donts: Don't put glass on widgets or stack glass on glass; use a solid card popover inside chrome.
Don't add title bars, drag handles or resize grips; the window manager stays hidden.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, a red error state, or teal fills beyond the soft selection wash.
Don't run slow ambient loops (breathing, drifting) on resting elements; the idle avatar blinks at random intervals instead.
Don't show a permanent taskbar; the dock appears only when it has something to show.
